purpose: Machine-checkable map of where a user opens licence texts offline inside the packaged client and inside an exported game. Paths are relative to the scan root. status values: required (must be present), required-when-engine-bundled (must be present only if the engine is actually bundled), conditional (must be present only if the named code is included), missing (not present today; a real gap), reference (repo-side official text, not expected in the package).

required.note: Byte-identical copy of vendor/pi-desktop/LICENSE (the LGPL-3 supplement). SHA-256 e3a994d82e644b03a792a930f574002658412f62407f5fee083f2555c5f23118.

required.reason: LGPL-3 incorporates GPL-3 by reference, so the full GPL-3 text ships with the LGPL supplement. Resolved from the official gnu.org text with URL, date and SHA-256 in texts/SOURCES.json.

The AGPL-3.0-only target is not applied: every covered entry is still pending-rights-review (unknown contributors, employer rights and upstream-derived files). Shipping an AGPL text would assert a licence the project has not established, so it is required only once a covered entry reaches status verified. Checked mechanically by licensing-check.mjs.

The MIT target for project export runtime/example code is not applied: the covered entries are pending-rights-review. It becomes required once a covered entry reaches status verified, so the project never ships a licence text it cannot yet grant. audio-models is not covered: it records that no audio or model asset is present, so it needs no project licence text.

required.note: Aggregate third-party notices; must be byte-identical to desktop/godot/licenses/GODOT_COPYRIGHT.txt.
Byte-identical to the upstream font licence.

Package-time inventory of installed npm packages; every listed licence file must exist beside it. repoText is the reference evidence, not a file to copy over the package inventory.

required.reason: Canonical MIT text, bundled so packages that ship no licence file still carry the notice.
Canonical Apache-2.0 text, bundled for npm and Rust dependencies under that licence.

Canonical BSD-3-Clause text, bundled for npm and Rust dependencies under that licence.

Canonical MPL-2.0 text is bundled; the source-availability condition of the MPL-2.0 dependencies remains an open legal question recorded in inventory.json.

Short licence text bundled for one installed package that ships no licence file of its own.
Generated from evidence/cargo-licenses.json at package time; it names every Rust crate, version and licence id and points at the canonical texts beside it.

required.note: Copied into every export by desktop/godot/export-probes.mjs; must stay byte-identical to desktop/godot/licenses/GODOT_LICENSE.txt.
Player-facing explanation of what may be done with an export and what must travel with it.

required.reason: The project MIT text for export runtime/example code is required once a covered entry reaches status verified; all covered entries are still pending-rights-review.
Required only if AGPL-licensed code is actually included in the exported game; that inclusion must be decided by the export pipeline, not assumed.
Required only if LGPL-licensed code is actually included in the exported game; the current export pipeline does not include the client.

rules: A text with status required must exist at root/file in the scanned tree.
required-when-engine-bundled is enforced only when the scan finds an engine binary or the engine notice path.

conditional is reported, never silently treated as satisfied or violated. When it carries condition 'covered-entries-verified', the checker fails if any covered inventory entry has status verified and the text is absent, and reports pending otherwise; this keeps a licence text out of the package until the project can actually grant it.
missing is a recorded gap: the check fails when a shipped component names it, and the report states the exact path a human must create.
reference entries are repo-side official texts under desktop/delivery/licensing/texts/ and are verified to exist there; they are not expected inside the package or export.
No path may be absolute or escape the scan root.
